feature_explanations.sslfinal_state: Assesses whether the HTTPS certificate is issued by a trustworthy Certificate Authority (e.g. VeriSign, GoDaddy) and has valid duration. Phishing sites typically lack trusted certificates or use self-signed certs.
feature_explanations.url_of_anchor: Measures the proportion of <a> anchor tags in the webpage pointing to an external domain or null javascript/empty hashes (#). Phishing pages often copy legitimate layouts but strip anchor links.
feature_explanations.prefix_suffix: Detects presence of dash symbols (-) in the domain name. Phishers frequently insert dashes (e.g., paypal-security.com) to impersonate trusted corporate brands.
feature_explanations.web_traffic: Measures domain web traffic ranking via Alexa / SimilarWeb. Legitimate popular websites rank high; disposable short-lived phishing sites have near-zero ranking.
feature_explanations.having_sub_domain: Counts domain dot hierarchy. Legitimate domains have 1 or 2 dots, whereas phishers use deep multi-level subdomains (e.g. verify.bank.com.phish.ru) to deceive users.
feature_explanations.links_in_tags: Examines the ratio of internal vs external URLs inside <meta>, <script>, and <link> tags. Phishing templates often hotlink legitimate site scripts to appear authentic.
feature_explanations.request_url: Calculates the percentage of external objects (images, videos, multimedia) loaded from an external domain. Phishers load media directly from the real brand domain.
feature_explanations.domain_registration_length: Checks if domain registration expires within 1 year. Over 90% of phishing domains are purchased on 1-year disposable contracts.
feature_explanations.sfh: Server Form Handler inspection. If an authentication form submits credentials to a blank URL ("about:blank") or external server, it is a high-risk credential harvester.
feature_explanations.having_ip_address: Checks if an IP address (or hexadecimal notation) is used directly instead of a domain name in the address bar (e.g. http://192.168.1.1/login.php).
